chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn 'Isa and Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

The woman with istihadah observes her menstrual days, so she does not perform salat (prayer) during them, and her husband does not approach her. When her days have passed and she sees that the blood pierces the cotton, she performs ghusl (ritual bath) for Zuhr and 'Asr, delaying this one and hastening that one, and for Maghrib and the later 'Isha' one ghusl, delaying this one and hastening that one; and she performs ghusl for Subh, stuffs herself with cotton, and binds herself tightly, and does not bend, and she presses her thighs together in the masjid while the rest of her body is outside. Her husband does not approach her during the days of her menstrual period. But if the blood does not pierce the cotton, she performs wudu (ablution), enters the masjid, and performs every salat (prayer) with wudu (ablution); and this one, her husband may approach her except during the days of her hayd.

key_terms.أَيَّامُهَا: her established menstrual days that determine the period of hayd
key_terms.الْكُرْسُفَ: cotton used to test or contain the bleeding
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the masjid, whose entry is discussed in relation to her state
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing irregular non-menstrual bleeding
key_terms.حَيْضِهَا: her menstruation, during which specific restrictions remain

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings for salat, ghusl, wudu, and marital relations for a woman with istihadah?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings for a woman experiencing istihadah, distinguishing between heavier and lighter bleeding based on whether the blood penetrates the cotton. It explains her obligations regarding ghusl, wudu, salat (prayer), entering the masjid, and marital relations, while preserving the separate rulings of hayd.
